prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: eight direction frames of ONE seeker drone dart: a small arrow-headed smart bullet with a lit thruster tail.

Design identity to keep exactly — a compact steel-grey arrow dart: a sharp triangular nose, short stubby wings, a round thruster nozzle at the tail burning hot amber (#f8a030 flame, #f8b048 core). One identical dart drawn eight times, each rotated to point its own of the eight compass directions; the lit thruster always trails opposite the nose.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 8 square cells laid out as 2 ROWS OF 4 (4-column by 2-row) — every cell holding exactly ONE subject; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = seeker dart pointing RIGHT (east) — horizontal, nose at the right The subject lies within aspect 1.0:1 to 2.45:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 2 = the SAME dart pointing lower-right (south-east, 45 degrees nose-down) The subject lies within aspect 0.5:1 to 1.92:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 3 = the SAME dart pointing DOWN (south, nose at the bottom, vertical) The subject lies within aspect 0.4:1 to 1.0:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 4 = the SAME dart pointing lower-left (south-west) The subject lies within aspect 0.5:1 to 1.92:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 5 = the SAME dart pointing LEFT (west, nose at the left) The subject lies within aspect 1.0:1 to 2.45:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 6 = the SAME dart pointing upper-left (north-west) The subject lies within aspect 0.5:1 to 1.92:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 7 = the SAME dart pointing UP (north, nose at the top, vertical) The subject lies within aspect 0.4:1 to 1.0:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
  cell 8 = the SAME dart pointing upper-right (north-east) The subject lies within aspect 0.5:1 to 1.92:1, identical scale and position as the other cells — only the named state changes.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 1024×512 px. Produce EXACTLY 8 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell and stays small — at least one quarter of the cell width is empty flat key to its left AND right, and the same above and below; a subject leaning on, touching or crossing a cell border ruins the whole sheet.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
- Every cell shows the SAME dart at the SAME size, perfectly CENTRED in its cell and COMPACT — each dart is only about 40% of the cell width; the other 60% stays flat green key. Only the pointing direction changes; the directions in reading order are exactly E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, N, NE — the diagonals point corner-to-corner at true 45 degrees, the cardinals perfectly level or vertical.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge
